final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim using the same record. That reframing is useful but not outcome-determinative. The policy text is explicit: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. The Actor now expressly concedes the opposite predicates remain unproven for the current release: the shelter-placement slice is below threshold, the release thread contains only an informal monitoring comment, and the record does not show current documentation, approved mitigation, approved acceptance, or disclosure text. That makes this more than a caveated but otherwise compliant position. A caveat can narrow an overbroad claim, but it cannot substitute for a mandatory certification condition that the available evidence still shows as missing. On the admissible record summarized here, the certification claim remains unsupported under policy, so the appropriate final verdict is noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows that current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
No new admissible evidence shows that the emergency shelter placement weakness is disclosed in current release materials.
No new admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance tied to the current release and this segment weakness.
Prior approval remains contextual only because the current release differs from the earlier approved release.
Aggregate readiness and rehearsal results support general launch readiness but do not satisfy the model-card certification predicates in policy.
